body:
Triage: lands in Studio's identifier derivation for New Package, New Object and Add Field (app-shell metadata-admin); rationale: a CJK display name derives nothing (blank required id, silently) or a positional `field_N` that becomes a permanent API name at publish. At minimum say so beside the identifier and never mint `field_N` without inviting a rename; transliteration is the fuller fix.
Path: studio · 不写代码建对象、字段 | studio-authoring.object-designer-roundtrip (P1, "identifiers derive…") | step ①
Grade: `priority:p2` — P1 bound from the item; a tax (the author can type an id), not a wall, so one step under.
Type: Bug
Dedupe: objectui search "Chinese display name identifier slug field_N pinyin" → no other hit.

Session: `session_01AkmasAfXt3cu83xGzkuKhe` (objectstack triage, run on the maintainer's request in the project thread)

Responsibility: objectui Studio's own create forms derive the identifier client side (`toFieldNameLoose`, `toIdSegment`), drop every non-Latin letter, and say nothing; no platform path covers it (the spec only states the identifier alphabet); every zh-CN author who types a Chinese label reaches it today
Thread-read: 6370409677
Serial constraints cleared: open objectui PRs read at claim time are #13395 (core ActionRunner), #13362, #13360, #13358 (workflows), #13289 (release), #13028 (timings data), #11845, #11844 (dependencies); none touches these paths. Open claims in this lane: #13384 (ActionRunner), #13350, #13349, #13348 (CI); none names these files.

Plan, stated so the review can hold it to it. Two parts:
- Part 1 (this PR, needed whichever way part 2 goes, since kana, Hangul, Arabic and other scripts derive nothing even with a transliteration): when a display name is filled in but yields no identifier, each surface says so beside the identifier and asks for one typed in Latin letters, instead of the "filled in from the display name" line or silence. Add field no longer mints a positional `field_N`: when the label yields no api name, or yields one another field already holds, the popover shows an API name box the author fills before Create. A Latin label behaves as today.
- Part 2 (transliteration of Chinese labels into a pinyin slug) is a product choice (a new client dependency and an identifier rule authors will see); it goes to the maintainer through the project's ruling flow and is not built before a ruling. Part 1's PR says `Refs`, not `Fixes`, until that ruling says whether part 2 is wanted.
- Out of this card's code: the `com.default.` package id prefix the card mentions is the active organization's slug (`default` on a fresh deployment); it is noted in the report, not changed here.
